summary: Sporting News previews the Week 11 college football game between North Texas (3-6, 1-4) and SMU (7-2, 5-0) on Friday at 9 p.m. ET on ESPN2. SMU is a heavy favorite, backed by a top-10 defense, a hot offense at home, and a four-year run of covering against North Texas, while North Texas has the nation's worst yardage defense. The writer picks SMU, with an Under lean if QB Preston Stone is sidelined by concussion protocol.
one_line: Sporting News previews SMU vs. North Texas, picking the red-hot 7-2 Mustangs as roughly two-touchdown favorites over a Mean Green defense that is the nation's worst in yards allowed.
key_facts: SMU is 7-2 overall and 5-0 in its final season in the American Athletic Conference, and has guaranteed its fifth consecutive winning season.
North Texas is 3-6, 1-4, has lost four of its past five games, and allows 37.4 points per game, ninth-worst in the nation.
The game kicks off Friday at 9 p.m. ET on ESPN2.
Over the previous four seasons SMU beat North Texas 48-10, 35-12, 65-35 and 49-27, covering the spread each time.
The line opened Mustangs -14 with a total of 71.5, and moved to 16 and 67.5 about 24 hours later; two of three models have SMU winning by 22 and 18 points.
SMU's defense allows 0.251 points per play (0.185 at home), while North Texas allows 0.501 points per play (0.533 on the road).
North Texas allows 479 yards per game, the worst in the country, and its past three opponents totaled 1,460 yards and 15 TDs.
SMU beat Tulsa 69-10 at homecoming two weeks earlier, leading 52-3 at halftime, the most Division I points in the first 30 minutes this year.
SMU sophomore QB Preston Stone threw for 1,171 yards in a four-game stretch, with 10 TDs and no interceptions in his past four games.
Stone left early in the fourth quarter at Rice after a hard hit; if concussion protocol sidelines him, redshirt freshman Kevin Jennings would start.
North Texas junior QB Chandler Jones had 19 TDs and no interceptions through seven games before throwing two picks in a 38-20 loss to UTSA.
BetRivers lists SMU to score first and win at Yes -165 and North Texas to score first and win at Yes +950; player props were not available.
The writer's pick is SMU, citing its home ball security (0.3 giveaways per game) and 49-51 percent pass/run balance.
